At that time, the great assembly, having heard the Buddha’s teaching, paid homage with deep respect; they followed the Buddha’s words, prostrated, and requested to withdraw.
Then Ānanda rose from his seat, joined his palms, knelt down, and said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!”
The Tathāgata has now fully explained all the bodily marks, yet alone has not revealed the mark of the invisible crown of the head.

We pray only that the World-Honored One will briefly describe the auspicious response of the light from this crown-mark, so that the ordinary and ignorant beings of future ages may come to know the supreme marks of the Buddha.

At that time, the World-Honored One entered the Samādhi of the Summit of the Crown, causing a lapis lazuli light to emerge from every single pore within the *uṣṇīṣa* (fleshly protuberance) atop the Buddha’s head. This light, like the spiral patterns on a conch shell, turned to the right and pervaded countless worlds throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of oceans equaling the atoms within ten billion worlds. From all eighty-four thousand pores of his body, there likewise issued forth these water-like manifestations;
each of these water manifestations, moreover, exceeded the aforementioned number by hundreds of thousands of millions of times beyond measure.

Upon these lapis lazuli waters grow numerous celestial jewel lotuses, each with hundreds of thousands of billions of petals; the petals display hundreds of thousands of billions of jewel colors, and even the smallest petals completely cover the trichiliocosm.
Upon each of these flowers, between every single filament, there were immeasurable, incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Ganges-sands of transformation Buddhas;
from the uṣṇīṣa-crowns of each of these transformation Buddhas, a multitude of rays of light likewise issued forth in the same manner.
At that time, the bodies of these Buddhas were equal in measure to space, such that they could not be measured;
thus, these Buddhas followed one after another, extending to the very limits of the ocean of worlds.

When this manifestation appeared, in each of the ten directions, there were Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion worlds, who ascended into the void and displayed great supernatural transformations as they arrived at the place where Śākyamuni Buddha was.

At that time, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, the bodhisattvas briefly beheld a small portion of auspicious signs within a single pore; immediately upon doing so, they each attained immeasurable hundreds of thousands of vajra-mark dhāraṇīs.
When the Buddha manifested this sign, the thousand bodhisattvas of the Bhadrakalpa and all the Buddhas of the ten directions likewise manifested this sign.
Among the great assembly present at that time, those who had attained the stage of *srotāpanna* became *arhats* in the space of a single *kṣaṇa*;
those who contemplate dependent origination became *arhats* by no longer relying on any conditions.
The Bodhisattva who has resolved their mind transcends all realms, furthering the ocean-gates of profound samādhi and abiding in the stage of nature;
the Bodhisattva of non-arising advances even more in immeasurable, supreme dharmas, abiding in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“In the turbid and evil world after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, if there are sentient beings who, upon hearing of the Buddha’s supreme marks, do not feel startled or doubtful, nor give rise to fear, you should know that such persons are able to extinguish all afflictions and karmic obstructions.”

Those who hear of the Buddha’s marks of excellence and give rise to sympathetic joy eliminate billions of kalpas of extremely heavy evil karma; in their future births, they shall not fall into the three miserable realms nor be born in the eight inopportune states.

When the Buddha had spoken these words, the elder Kauṇḍinya and the other great bhikṣus, Maitreya and the other great bodhisattvas, and the immeasurable multitude, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they received it upon their heads and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Ocean-like Samādhi of Contemplating the Buddha, Scroll Ten.
